The module base has five large rounded cutouts, reducing solid CAD volume by about 37% while retaining the mounting pads, diagonal webs and flat printing underside. The rotating deck now has five R3-cornered windows, reducing its solid CAD volume by 25.2% while retaining the bearing hub, six radial ribs, outer rim and full Z-cradle mounting footprints. Only the rotating deck needs reprinting for this latest update. Four 625ZZ rollers tilt 45° on integral printed axles, with one rounded block each and no roller bolts or nuts. They run on the 176 mm ring's continuous outer bevel, clear of its flat-seated button-head screws. The bearing spindle is Ø15.25 mm with a 0.5 mm top chamfer. The module plate retains its flat underside. Left drag orbits, middle drag pans, and the wheel zooms; right-click opens the menu. The Z stage keeps 2 mm above the centre clamp at full retraction. Its solid top mounting face and side wall join continuously along the corner. The one-piece cradle uses six M4 flange bolts into threaded deck inserts. The U-shaped carrier covers the Z rack output pad and clamps both sides with four M3×35 bolts, nuts and eight washers, giving eight carrier contact points without output inserts. Both stages use R24 rear pass-through enclosures. The radial stage bolts upward through the carrier shelf into its four downward-facing reinforced posts. Four tips target a 2 × 2 mm cluster. Base and Z NEMA17 bodies: 48 mm. Radial NEMA14 body: 34 mm. Tapered extensions keep the wider probe holders apart. The upper motor stays centered over the base rotation axis. The platform is 700 × 700 mm to accommodate the longer output rack and tapered probe mount.

The inner 12T base pinion uses open tooth slots with full-width spring walls and no small finger caps, meshing with the 72T internal ring for 6:1 reduction. The motor is mounted 60 mm from the rotation axis. At 1/16 microstepping, tip movement is 0.082 mm at board center and 0.103 mm at maximum reach; actual accuracy remains unmeasured.

Green translucent volumes reserve space for the rear controller components and USB cables. Component height, spacers and cables are provisional allowances. Load capacity, stiffness, contact force, print fit and accuracy remain untested. The checked module explosion separates one arm, removes the radial bottom-mount screws, and opens its lids. Actuator drives stay assembled; switch to Four arms for coordinated probing.

Based on FLEX, compliant-spur-gear, and the RP2040 motor controller.
